s763.content:
Antônio de Sant’Anna Galvão, born in Guaratinguetá in the state of São Paulo, became a Franciscan friar and a sought-after confessor and preacher. With Sister Helena Maria he founded the Recolhimento da Luz, a house for women in São Paulo, and spent decades building its church and convent.

He is remembered for the “Frei Galvão pills,” tiny papers bearing a prayer to Our Lady, which the sick still take with faith. In 2007 Benedict XVI canonized him in São Paulo, the first saint born in Brazil.
s763.intercession: St. Frei Galvão, pray for us, and for all who are sick. Amen.

s764.content:
Amabile Visintainer was born in Trentino and emigrated as a child with her family to southern Brazil. In 1890, with a friend, she began caring for a woman dying of cancer in a small house in Vígolo, the start of the Little Sisters of the Immaculate Conception.

As Mother Paulina she led the congregation, but she was later removed as superior and spent her last decades in humble work and prayer, often in pain. John Paul II canonized her in 2002, the first saint to have lived in Brazil.
s764.intercession: St. Paulina, pray for us. Teach us to serve without being seen. Amen.

s765.content:
José de Anchieta, born in the Canary Islands, joined the Jesuits at Coimbra and was sent to Brazil at nineteen. He helped found the mission school around which the city of São Paulo grew, and wrote a grammar of the Tupi language, with plays, poems, and catechisms for the native peoples.

He served as a peacemaker between colonists and native nations and as provincial of the Jesuits in Brazil, and is called the Apostle of Brazil. Pope Francis canonized him in 2014.
s765.intercession: St. José de Anchieta, pray for us, and for all who teach the faith. Amen.

s766.content:
Roque González de Santa Cruz, born in Asunción, was a diocesan priest who joined the Jesuits to work among the Guaraní. He founded several reductions, mission towns where the Guaraní lived protected from slave raiders, farming and worshiping together.

In 1628 he and two Spanish Jesuits, Alonso Rodríguez and Juan del Castillo, were killed at the instigation of a local shaman. John Paul II canonized them in Asunción in 1988.
s766.intercession: Holy Martyrs of Paraguay, pray for us, and for all native peoples. Amen.

s767.content:
Carlos Manuel Rodríguez, called Charlie, was a layman of Caguas, Puerto Rico, whose poor health kept him from finishing university. Working as an office clerk, he spent his wages and free time teaching the faith, especially to students.

He loved the liturgy and promoted its renewal long before the Second Vatican Council, speaking above all of the Easter Vigil: “We live for that night.” He died of cancer at forty-four and was beatified in 2001, the first Puerto Rican to be beatified.
s767.intercession: Blessed Carlos Manuel, pray for us. Fill us with the joy of Easter. Amen.

s768.content:
Tshimangadzo Samuel Daswa, of the Lemba people of Limpopo in South Africa, became a Catholic as a young man and took the name Benedict. He was a school principal, a husband and father of eight, and a leader in his parish.

When his village blamed lightning strikes on witchcraft and collected money to pay a witch doctor, he refused to take part and spoke against it. On February 2, 1990, he was ambushed and killed. He was beatified in 2015, the first South African to be beatified.
s768.intercession: Blessed Benedict Daswa, pray for us. Free us from fear, and keep us faithful. Amen.

s769.content:
Victor, an African, was bishop of Rome from about 189 to 199. He is remembered for the dispute over the date of Easter: he wished all the churches to keep it on Sunday, as Rome did, and threatened to break communion with the churches of Asia, which kept it on the fourteenth of Nisan, until St. Irenaeus urged him toward peace.

St. Jerome counts him among the first Church writers in Latin.
s769.intercession: St. Victor, pray for us, and for the unity of the Church. Amen.

s770.content:
Marcellus was a Roman centurion. In 298, during a feast for the emperors’ birthday, he threw down his soldier’s belt before the standards, declaring that he served Christ the eternal King and could no longer serve the emperors.

He was tried at Tingis, now Tangier, by the deputy prefect Agricolanus and beheaded. The acts of his trial are among the oldest records of the martyrs.
s770.intercession: St. Marcellus, pray for us. Make us loyal to Christ our King. Amen.

s771.content:
Fructuosus, bishop of Tarragona in Spain, was arrested with his deacons Augurius and Eulogius under the emperor Valerian, and they were burned alive in the amphitheater on January 21, 259.

The acts of their martyrdom tell that when a Christian asked him for his prayers, Fructuosus answered that he must keep in mind the whole Catholic Church, spread from east to west. St. Augustine preached on their feast.
s771.intercession: Sts. Fructuosus, Augurius, and Eulogius, pray for us, and for the whole Church. Amen.

s772.content:
Justa and Rufina were sisters of Seville who made and sold pottery. According to their acts, they refused to sell their wares for a pagan festival and broke an image of the goddess carried in procession, for which they were imprisoned and tortured.

Justa died in prison, and Rufina was strangled. They are the patrons of Seville and of potters, and tradition says they protect the Giralda tower.
s772.intercession: Sts. Justa and Rufina, pray for us, and bless the work of our hands. Amen.

s773.content:
María Maravillas Pidal y Chico de Guzmán, born in Madrid to a noble family, entered the Discalced Carmelites at El Escorial in 1919. In 1924 she founded a Carmel at the Cerro de los Ángeles, beside the monument to the Sacred Heart at the center of Spain.

She founded or restored many more Carmels in Spain and one in India, living strict enclosure while quietly helping to build homes and schools for the poor. John Paul II canonized her in 2003.
s773.intercession: St. Maravillas, pray for us. Teach us to do whatever God wants. Amen.

s774.content:
Maddalena of Canossa, a marchioness of Verona, left the life of her family’s palace to serve the poor, beginning with the neglected girls of the city’s poorest district. In 1808 she founded the Daughters of Charity, known as the Canossian Sisters, to teach, catechize, and care for the sick.

She later founded a branch for men, the Sons of Charity. John Paul II canonized her in 1988.
s774.intercession: St. Maddalena, pray for us, and for all who teach the poor. Amen.

s775.content:
Luigi Guanella, a priest of the diocese of Como, spent his life for those no one else would take in: people with disabilities, the elderly poor, and orphans. He founded the Servants of Charity and the Daughters of St. Mary of Providence, and his houses spread from Italy to the United States.

He trusted in God’s providence for everything his houses needed. Benedict XVI canonized him in 2011.
s775.intercession: St. Luigi Guanella, pray for us, and for all who live with disabilities. Amen.

s776.content:
Giovanni Calabria, a poor shoemaker’s son of Verona, was a seminarian when he found an abandoned boy in the street on a cold night in 1897 and took him in. From that night grew the Poor Servants of Divine Providence, who care for orphans, the sick, and the poor, trusting entirely in providence.

He longed for unity among Christians and wrote to many, among them the Anglican writer C. S. Lewis, in Latin. John Paul II canonized him in 1999.
s776.intercession: St. Giovanni Calabria, pray for us, and for children without homes. Amen.

s777.content:
Annibale Di Francia, a priest of Messina, went to live among the poor of the slum of Avignone, caring for orphans and families in misery. Taking to heart the words of Jesus, “Pray therefore the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest,” he made prayer for vocations the mark of his work.

He founded the Rogationists and the Daughters of Divine Zeal. John Paul II canonized him in 2004.
s777.intercession: St. Annibale, pray for us, and ask the Lord of the harvest to send laborers. Amen.

s778.content:
Anna Maria Redi of Arezzo entered the Discalced Carmel of Florence at seventeen. Pondering the words “God is love,” she gave herself to a hidden love of God and to tireless, unnoticed service of her sisters, especially the sick in the infirmary.

She died suddenly at twenty-two. Pius XI canonized her in 1934.
s778.intercession: St. Teresa Margaret, pray for us. Teach us to love in hidden ways. Amen.

s779.content:
Ignatius of Laconi, a peasant’s son of Sardinia, joined the Capuchins and for forty years was the friary’s questing brother in Cagliari, going door to door begging for the friars and the poor.

He was loved for his gentleness and his care for the sick and for children, and many healings were credited to his prayers. Pius XII canonized him in 1951.
s779.intercession: St. Ignatius of Laconi, pray for us. Make us humble and kind. Amen.

s780.content:
Pietro Fioretti, a shoemaker of Viterbo, entered the Capuchins as a lay brother, taking the name Crispin. He served as cook, gardener, and for many years as questor in Orvieto, begging alms for his friars.

Cheerful and full of wit, he called himself the little donkey of the Capuchins and loved Our Lady deeply. He was the first saint canonized by John Paul II, in 1982.
s780.intercession: St. Crispin, pray for us. Give us cheerful hearts. Amen.

s781.content:
Takayama Ukon, a Japanese lord baptized as a boy with the name Justo, ruled the castle town of Takatsuki and helped the faith spread there. When the ruler Toyotomi Hideyoshi ordered him in 1587 to give up Christianity, he chose to lose his lands and rank instead.

After decades of quiet faith, he was exiled in 1614 with other Christians to Manila, where he died weeks after arriving, early in 1615. Pope Francis beatified him as a martyr in 2017.
s781.intercession: Blessed Justo, pray for us. Keep us faithful when it costs us. Amen.

s782.content:
Cosmas, an orphan, was raised in Damascus in the household of St. John Damascene’s father, and the two grew up as brothers and studied together. Both became monks of the Lavra of St. Sabbas near Jerusalem.

Cosmas became bishop of Maiuma, near Gaza. He wrote canons for the great feasts that the Byzantine churches still sing, among them the Christmas canon that begins, “Christ is born, give glory!”
s782.intercession: St. Cosmas, pray for us, and teach us to sing God’s praise. Amen.

s783.content:
Theodore Stratelates, “the General,” was a Christian commander at Heraclea on the Black Sea. According to his acts, he broke the gold and silver idols that the emperor Licinius had sent to be honored and gave the pieces to the poor, and he was tortured and crucified.

The Byzantine churches honor him as a great-martyr on February 8, beside his namesake St. Theodore Tyro.
s783.intercession: Holy Great-Martyr Theodore, pray for us. Amen.

s784.content:
Macrina, a disciple of St. Gregory the Wonderworker, endured the persecution of Diocletian with her husband, hiding for years in the forests of Pontus.

She was the grandmother of Sts. Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa, Peter of Sebaste, and Macrina the Younger. Basil wrote that she taught him the faith as a child, passing on the words of Gregory.
s784.intercession: St. Macrina, pray for us, and for all grandparents. Amen.

s785.content:
Jeremiah was called as a young man to prophesy in Jerusalem in the last years before the Babylonians destroyed the city in 587 BC. He warned the kings and people to turn back to God, and was mocked, beaten, imprisoned, and thrown into a cistern.

In the darkest hour he foretold a new covenant: “I will put my law within them, and I will write it upon their hearts.” After the fall of Jerusalem he was taken to Egypt. The Byzantine churches also honor him on May 1.
s785.intercession: Holy Prophet Jeremiah, pray for us, and for all who suffer for speaking the truth. Amen.

s786.content:
Elisha was plowing in his father’s field when Elijah threw his mantle over him, and he left everything to follow him. When Elijah was taken up into heaven, Elisha asked for a double share of his spirit and took up his mantle.

He healed the Syrian general Naaman of leprosy in the waters of the Jordan, a story Jesus recalled, and raised the son of the woman of Shunem. The Byzantine churches also honor him on June 14.
s786.intercession: Holy Prophet Elisha, pray for us. Amen.

s787.content:
Daniel was one of the young men of Judah taken to Babylon, where he served at the court of the kings, refused food that would break God’s law, and interpreted dreams by God’s wisdom. For praying to God against the king’s decree he was thrown into the lions’ den and kept unharmed.

His visions include “one like a son of man” coming with the clouds of heaven, the title Jesus took for himself. The Byzantine churches honor him with the Three Holy Youths on December 17.
s787.intercession: Holy Prophet Daniel, pray for us. Keep us faithful in a strange land. Amen.

s788.content:
Samuel was the son Hannah begged of God and gave back to him, raised as a boy at the sanctuary of Shiloh. When the Lord called him in the night, he answered, “Speak, for thy servant hears.”

As prophet and the last of the judges of Israel, he anointed Saul as the first king, and later, at God’s word, anointed the shepherd boy David. The Byzantine churches also honor him on August 20.
s788.intercession: Holy Prophet Samuel, pray for us. Help us to listen when God calls. Amen.

s789.content:
God called Abraham to leave his country and his father’s house and go to a land he would be shown, promising to make of him a great nation in whom all the families of the earth would be blessed. He went, trusting the promise even when he and Sarah were old and childless, and Isaac was born to them.

Asked to offer Isaac, he obeyed, and God provided. St. Paul calls him the father of all who believe, and the Roman Canon names him “our father in faith.” The Roman Martyrology remembers him on October 9.
s789.intercession: Holy Abraham, pray for us. Give us your faith. Amen.

s790.content:
Zechariah was a priest serving in the Temple when the angel Gabriel appeared to him and promised that his wife Elizabeth, old and barren, would bear a son. Because he doubted, he was struck dumb until the child was born.

When he wrote, “His name is John,” his tongue was freed, and he praised God in the canticle the Church still sings each morning, the Benedictus. The Byzantine churches honor him on September 5.
s790.intercession: St. Zechariah, pray for us. Open our lips to praise God. Amen.

s791.content:
Joseph Marmion, a priest of Dublin, entered the Benedictine abbey of Maredsous in Belgium in 1886, taking the name Columba, and became its abbot in 1909.

His conferences, gathered in books such as Christ, the Life of the Soul, taught that the whole spiritual life is to live as children of God in Christ, and they were loved by priests and religious across the world. John Paul II beatified him in 2000.
s791.intercession: Blessed Columba, pray for us. Help us to live in Christ. Amen.

s792.content:
Pauline Jaricot, a young woman of Lyon, gathered workers in groups of ten who each gave a sou a week and prayed for the missions. Her idea grew into the Society for the Propagation of the Faith, which still supports missions worldwide.

She also founded the Living Rosary, in which fifteen people each pray one decade a day. She lost her fortune in a failed project to help workers and died poor. She was beatified in Lyon in 2022.
s792.intercession: Blessed Pauline, pray for us, and for the missions. Amen.

s793.content:
Engelmar Unzeitig, a German-speaking Moravian, was a priest of the Mariannhill Missionaries. Arrested in 1941 for preaching in defense of the Jews, he was sent to Dachau, where he learned Russian to serve prisoners from the East.

In the winter of 1944–1945 he volunteered to nurse the prisoners dying of typhus, caught it himself, and died on March 2, 1945. He is called the Angel of Dachau. He was beatified in 2016.
s793.intercession: Blessed Engelmar, pray for us. Teach us to love without counting the cost. Amen.

s794.content:
Józef Ulma, a farmer, photographer, and beekeeper of Markowa in Poland, and his wife Wiktoria hid eight Jews in their home during the German occupation.

On March 24, 1944, German police shot the Jews they sheltered and then the whole Ulma family: Józef, Wiktoria, who was pregnant, and their seven children. They were beatified together in 2023, the unborn child among them. Their feast is kept on July 7, the anniversary of their marriage.
s794.intercession: Blessed Ulma family, pray for us, and for all families. Amen.

s795.content:
Hanna Chrzanowska of Kraków trained as a nurse and gave her life to nursing, teaching it and writing on it. In her later years she built up care for the chronically ill in their homes, sending nurses and volunteers to visit the forgotten sick of the city.

She worked closely with Karol Wojtyła, then archbishop of Kraków, who preached at her funeral. She was beatified in Kraków in 2018.
s795.intercession: Blessed Hanna, pray for us, and for nurses and all who care for the sick. Amen.

s796.content:
Karolina Kózka was a peasant girl of Wał-Ruda near Tarnów in Poland, known for teaching the catechism to the children of her village and for her love of the Rosary.

On November 18, 1914, during the First World War, a Russian soldier led her into the forest to assault her. She resisted and fled, and he killed her. She was sixteen. John Paul II beatified her in Tarnów in 1987.
s796.intercession: Blessed Karolina, pray for us, and for all young people. Amen.

s797.content:
Michał Sopoćko was a priest and professor of Vilnius and the confessor of St. Faustina Kowalska. Testing her visions carefully, he came to believe them, and in 1934 he had the first image of the Divine Mercy painted.

He spent the rest of his life making known the devotion to the Divine Mercy and founded the congregation that became the Sisters of Merciful Jesus. He died in Białystok in 1975 and was beatified there in 2008.
s797.intercession: Blessed Michał, pray for us. Jesus, I trust in You. Amen.

s798.content:
Stanislaus Papczyński left the Piarists, where he had taught and preached, to found a new community: the Marian Fathers of the Immaculate Conception, the first order of men founded in Poland, approved in 1699.

He asked his priests to honor the Immaculate Conception, to pray for the souls in purgatory, and to help parish priests with preaching. He died on September 17, 1701, and Pope Francis canonized him in 2016.
s798.intercession: St. Stanislaus Papczyński, pray for us, and for the holy souls. Amen.

s799.content:
Rupert, a Frankish bishop of Worms, came to Bavaria around 696 at the invitation of Duke Theodo. At the ruins of the Roman town of Juvavum he founded St. Peter’s Abbey and, with his niece St. Erentrude, the convent of Nonnberg, and the city of Salzburg grew around them.

He encouraged the salt works that gave the city its name. He is the patron of Salzburg, and Austria keeps his feast on September 24.
s799.intercession: St. Rupert, pray for us, and for the people of Austria. Amen.

s800.content:
Adolph Kolping worked as a journeyman shoemaker before studying for the priesthood. Ordained in 1845, he saw how young craftsmen wandering from town to town were left without home or faith.

He gathered them into Catholic journeymen’s associations, with houses where they could live, learn, and pray, and they spread through Germany and beyond as today’s Kolping movement. He died in Cologne in 1865 and was beatified in 1991.
s800.intercession: Blessed Adolph Kolping, pray for us, and for all who work. Amen.

s801.content:
Niels Stensen, called Steno, was a Danish anatomist who made discoveries about glands, the heart, and the brain, and laid the foundations of geology, seeing that the layers of the earth record its history.

In Florence he was received into the Catholic Church in 1667. He became a priest and then a bishop serving the scattered Catholics of northern Germany and Scandinavia, living in great poverty. He died in Schwerin in 1686 and was beatified in 1988.
s801.intercession: Blessed Niels, pray for us, and for all who study God’s creation. Amen.

s802.content:
Zygmunt Gorazdowski, a priest of Lviv who suffered from poor health all his life, became known as the father of the poor. He opened a shelter for beggars, a public kitchen, a home for single mothers and abandoned infants, and a school.

To carry on this work he founded the Sisters of Mercy of St. Joseph. He died on January 1, 1920, and Benedict XVI canonized him in 2005.
s802.intercession: St. Zygmunt, pray for us, and for the poor of every city. Amen.
